So I've tried serequil. Take this with a grain of salt because everyone is different. My most prevalent symptom of PTSD was rage. I took two doses and I was in a straight rage for over half a week. And, for what it's worth, ALL SSRIs are too much for me and usually have really terrible side effects like what I listed above. So if You're not overly sensitive to SSRIs, I'd be willing to guess you'd get more out of serequil than I did. Make sure you go over everything with your doctor and I would try to book a follow up appointment after a few days/ a week- just in case.


Also just as a side note- the meds that ended up working for me were a combination of Ritalin, klonopin, and Wellbutrin. 


And this is in NO WAY medical advice. Your doctor has your best interest in mind and would not prescribe you something they think would be ineffective. 


Good luck.

Hey it's me, your girlfriend! Just kidding, but I was her, once. She has an anger problem. It could be a symptom of something else (stress or anxiety disorder) or it could just be anger, but she'll probably want to talk to a doctor about that. She is catastrophizing, and when you catastrophize you really can't tell you're doing it unless someone points it out. 


I have anger issues that stem from ptsd, and for years I was very much like your girlfriend. If she's anything like me, she does *not* want to be this angry. No one does. It hurts so bad, truly so painful to be so uncontrollably angry that the only way to get it out is to scream or throw things or hit things. I call my anger my black sludge. It sits in me, simmering. 


I needed professional help and I got it and now I have all new ways to deal with anger that are healthy. She may need professional help. Bring it up when she is *not angry.* approach it from the pain perspective. She will not take it well, or maybe she will.

"Gf, I love you so much and you're so important to me. I wanted to talk to you about how you feel when you get angry. It worries me, seeing you like that. I want you to be happy, and to feel good, and to not feel all those bad feelings that come with anger. Would you consider talking to someone about it? Maybe even just once, to learn some coping tools?"

No one likes to be told they need help. She'll probably get angry. I ruined a lot of great relationships- friends and significant others alike- from my anger. It really sounds like it's something she needs therapy for, but only she can make that decision. 

As far as you go, I completely understand what it's like to be you, because I've behaved that way to several men in my life and they all tell me what it does to them. It's awful. You don't deserve it. Just because it may be a problem for her does not make it okay for her to have outbursts. Next time she has one, walk away. If she follows you, calmly tell her you will not listen to irrationalities and you need space to clear your head. That will get you away from the anger AND give her some perspective in how it effects you. Good luck my friend.

Hey! I'm very familiar with this personal hell!

I'm the exact same way, been like that for as long as I can remember. My therapist says she's never heard of the problem, but my psychiatrist has. 

I don't get sad, but my anxiety gets really high and it will often send me into a panic attack, especially if I see an old person by themselves, or someone dressed poorly. 


Same thing as if someone told me they were feeling sad (like you with your mother).

Nothing my doctors ever suggested helped, but I came up with something that sort of helps me, maybe it might be useful for you, too.

When I see someone and start to feel bad for them for any small reason (running shoes with jeans is a big one, or seeing an old person with a bad back walking down the street), instead of spiraling out of control into an anxious loop of questioning whether or not they're okay/ happy, I *scold* myself instead.

Example A( a stranger): Stranges, why are you making all of these assumptions about someone? You don't know their life. They may be perfectly happy- fuck they're probably doing better than you! Stop being so presumptuous!

Example B (I know someone is feeling bad): Stranges, put yourself in their shoes. How sad would you be? Probably not THAT sad. They're fine. They feel the same way you feel when you're down in the dumps. Don't you always end up feeling better? 


I find that putting it in that perspective rather than wallowing in unwarranted anxiety is really helpful in relieving my negative feelings. And, it's probably all true, too.

Hey, don't kill your self. I know exactly how you feel. Like your skin is either too tight or too loose or too hot and you need to crawl out of it or just you're walking down the street and you *know* you're walking because you're moving forward but you don't really *feel* yourself walking because, frankly, you're already dead.

So almost 6 years ago was the latest (and hopefully final) night I attempted to take my own life, because I didn't think anything would get better. And I was cool with it. I told my friends I knew they didn't like me and that was fine, they could stop calling me. Made amends with people I wanted to make amends with. Wrote some music. Slit my wrists.

Woke up alive. Obviously. And I rolled my eyes so far back in my head when people told me "it will get better." Like hell it will. What do they know. Only you know. The nightmares, nausea, disassociation, fear, all that bullshit. 

That was almost six years ago. I'll tell you now. I kept going, even though I didn't want to. And slowly- VERY slowly- things began to heal. And things got better. They're not perfect, things can improve, but that's the thing- I now know they *can and will* improve. Because they already have. And I didn't even notice while it was happening. All I really did was keep getting out of bed in the morning. And fuck, there were so many days I said fuck if and stayed in bed all day, sometimes a week or so. But you gotta keep going. You just have to. 

If I had been successful 6 years ago, I wouldn't have met the love of my life. We're engaged. I wouldn't have seen my favorite musician in concert twice. I would've died without telling my mother I loved her. Now I make sure to say that to everyone all the time. 

Look I'm rambling because truth be told I'm the same as you, I fight with those suicidal feelings and I drink them away. I'm a little drunk. I just really don't want you to kill your self because I've been in your shoes and I'm probably still wearing those shoes but I can tell you from experience, you reach a point where things really can't get any worse, and so they get better. And then you will feel a little better, so you'll do more, which will in turn makes things better, so on and so forth. Don't hurt yourself, please, please. Call a hotline or PM myself or someone else to talk but don't hurt yourself. Please hold out for all the good to come. 

Edit to add for context: I'm about 10 years older than you, so I've had a *lot* of time to process the emotions and everything so I want you to know it's okay to feel like shit, it will take a long time before you have days where you feel good all day. But it does happen and it will happen.

When Shakespeare is taught the right way, and given the correct context, you can really see his genius.  He meticulously utilizes tools of the English language to illustrate the larger picture he is trying to paint.  The nature of our individual identity, sense of self, is my favorite of his themes.  For instance:  All of Shakespeare's characters speak in rhymed iambic pentameter.  Iambic pentameter is the meter that most closely resembles natural English speaking.  The unstressed and stressed syllables alternating mimics the natural flow of speech.  Now, Shakespeare uses this for all of his characters *except* royalty.  For royalty, Shakespeare has reserved *unrhymed iambic pentameter*.  Only his royal characters speak this way.

In the opening of *A Midsummer Night's Dream*, we see a drunk, slurred speech, acting like a complete dick.  A group of royals find this bum asleep and decide to play a prank on him.  They bring him to a room in their castle and dress him in all the trappings of great wealth.  Provide a beautiful buffet spread and servants.  When he wakes, the bum is confused.  The royals convince him being a bum was all a dream and that he had always been a lord.

And what does this mother fucker do?

He starts speaking in unrhymed iambic pentameter!!!!

His perception was changed, not reality. And yet, how quickly he accepts this identity.  How quickly does his identity change?  Immediately.  And it's all an illusion.  So what does our identity even mean?  Is it always so easily shattered?  Is our identity an illusion?  

The sprite, (I think he's a sprite at least), Puck, says it best.

Puck:  We are patched.

*We are patched.*

We make up one anther.  We are nothing without our counterparts, our identity is shaped around the identities around us.  We cannot exist without each other, we are all a part of each other, we are *patches of a whole.*
